notes: THE FIVE DOORS (Dean, 02/09/2026, v31). This file is the one place that says what each suit's action IS. Everything else in the game reads it from here, and there are now exactly two readers: a suit's NOTICE BOARD grants the action to whoever places a card on it, and a MEEPLE of that colour performs the same action, free, when its owner spends it at the start of a turn. Same five entries, same five actions, two ways in.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31. What left the file in one edit: serviceThreshold, ownerActivationCost and visitWage, plus every enhancement the roster carried. If you are reading a note or a report written before 02/09/2026 that mentions a Service starter, a hire fee, a Working Week, a wage ladder or an enhanced door, it is describing a game that no longer exists.

THERE IS NO SERVICE CARD, AND NOW THERE IS NO SERVICE. The fourth starter went on 20/08/2026 when the door merged into the Notice Board; the last of its vocabulary goes here. serviceThreshold is deleted because the door's threshold is the Notice Board's, printed on the card and overridden by rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold, and one number in two files is how the 5-versus-2 drift happened the first time. ownerActivationCost is deleted because there is nothing to pay it with and, more to the point, because the owner is no longer a special case: in v31 the owner places a card on their own board exactly as a rival does, threshold and all. visitWage is deleted because there are no coins to mint - the payment to the owner was already 0 and already the FREIGHT, which is the one part of the old economy that survives intact.

THE DOORS ARE PLAIN, AND THAT IS THE CHANGE. Every entry below performs its suit's action exactly as the core action performs it, with one marked exception. The enhancements the doors used to carry (a relaxed harvest, a hand card into the barn before a delivery, a deck-sown card, a build at a discount of 2 with the crop requirements waived) are all gone. The reason is that the bonus slot itself became the enhancement: a door now buys a WHOLE CORE ACTION for one card, which is a far bigger prize than any of those riders ever was, and stacking a rider on top of it was pricing a sweetener into a deal that no longer needed one. It also collapses five paragraphs of teach into one sentence - 'place a card, take that suit's action' - which is what a five-minute teach is for.

THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE ORCHARD DOOR, AT DRAW 3, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The self-cancellation law is the reason: a visitor pays 1 card to use a door, so a door whose action PRODUCES cards has to over-deliver or buying it is net zero. In v31 the yardstick got higher, because the bonus slot's other option is a free Draw 1 (rules.turn.bonusDraw). A plain Draw 2 door would cost 1 card and return 2, netting +1 - exactly what the free option gives for nothing - so it would be STRICTLY WORSE than the alternative and the Orchard board would take no traffic at all. Draw 3 nets +2: pay your worst card, draw three, and the door is card-positive against the free option by one card. That is the whole margin the door has. If anybody ever tidies this to Draw 2 for consistency with the other four, the Orchard door dies overnight, and it will die silently - nothing will error, the traffic will simply go somewhere else. overlays/orchard-door-draw-two-v1.overlay.json is the paired control that measures exactly this.

THE APIARY DOOR SOWS FROM THE HAND, AND IT IS THE WEAKEST DOOR ON THE TABLE (Dean, 02/09/2026, ruled that way knowingly). A visitor pays 1 card onto the board and then spends a SECOND card sowing, for 1 threshold step on one of their own buildings: 2 cards out for one step in. That is the self-cancellation law biting on the one door where it was not paid off. The old fix was to sow off a deck top, which cost the visitor nothing extra and had the better theme besides - the pollinator carries something in from elsewhere. It was dropped for v31 because a plain action is a plain action and the exception budget was spent on Orchard. MEASURE THE DOOR MIX FIRST. If the Apiary board takes no traffic, the fix is to move the sown card back to a deck top (`from: 'deck'`), not to make the door cheaper.

A MEEPLE IS THE SAME ACTION WITHOUT THE CARD. It is drawn face up onto an island delivery space at setup, claimed with that delivery, spent one at a time at the start of a later turn, and then leaves the game for good. A meeple of a suit that is NOT at the table still works, which is why this file lists all five entries regardless of the seat count and why island.json deals its bag from all five colours: the five actions exist independently of who farms what. The colour-to-action map is therefore here and nowhere else, and island.json says so explicitly rather than copying it.

RULING (carried over, unchanged since v13): suit powers apply to actions performed through a door or by a meeple. It is your action, whoever's premises it is taken on and whatever wooden thing paid for it.

`name` IS FLAVOUR ONLY. These five names were printed on the Service cards that no longer exist, and nothing in v31 prints them - the door is printed on the Notice Board and the meeple is a colour. They are kept because the UI and the reports read better with a name than with an action id, and because renaming them is a design decision this file is not entitled to make on its own. Treat them as labels awaiting a ruling, not as card titles.

linkedSuit is ownership in the door sense: the seat playing that suit owns that Notice Board and nobody else does, so the table's menu of buyable actions is decided by which suits were chosen. It is NOT ownership in the meeple sense - anybody may hold and spend a meeple of any colour.
unresolved: THE ORCHARD EXCEPTION IS THE ONE ASYMMETRY IN AN OTHERWISE FLAT SET, and it is defended by arithmetic rather than by measurement. The arithmetic is sound (Draw 2 ties the free option, Draw 3 beats it by one card) but nobody has yet run the arm that shows the Orchard board taking MORE traffic than the other four in proportion, which is what would say the margin is right rather than merely non-zero. If Orchard runs away with the door mix, the dial is this number and not the Orchard suit's cards.
The Apiary door's hand-sow, above. Ruled, not settled.

Whether a door should ever refuse a visitor who cannot use it. A Wheat door with no full building to harvest, a Vegetable door with an empty barn, a Dairy door with nothing affordable: the visitor pays a card and gets nothing. In v30 that was rare, because the doors were enhanced and the enhancements mostly applied; with plain actions it is a live case at every board. Nothing in the data expresses a legality check, and the engine will have to rule it one way or the other.

A10 The Cross-Pollinator printed 'HIRE a Hired Worker, paying GBP 1 less', which has been text for a rule that does not exist since 2026-08-10 and is now text for a currency that does not exist either. It is a card, so it belongs to the sheet and to cards.json, but it is recorded here because this file is where the referent died.
